examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: A partial order is reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive. Its Hasse diagram omits reflexive and transitively implied edges. For linear extensions, repeatedly choose a currently minimal remaining element; different such choices generate distinct total orders. Count using recursion on the remaining subset, not arbitrary permutations that may violate a dependency.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
On {a,b,c,d}, the only nontrivial constraints are a<c and b<c. How many linear extensions exist?

**Answer: 8.** Among a,b,c, c must come last, leaving 2 orders for a,b. The unrelated d can be inserted in any of 4 positions. Total=2·4=8.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Minimal means no strictly smaller element exists; least means it is below every element. A partial order can have several minimal elements and no least element.

A maximal element need not be a greatest element; do not infer comparability from vertical position alone.
